controller.label: Arduino Uno R3 + CNC Shield V3
controller.spec: 4 x A4988 (X, Y, Z, A); A axis on D12/D13 via the two A-jumpers; EN D8 (all drivers); USB-B to the computer

pins.signal: USB-B to the computer (115200 baud, firmware arm_v4)

psu.label: 24 V 6 A supply (owned)
psu.spec: 24 V DC, 6 A, barrel plug; unplugging it is the e-stop (lower the arm first)

components.label: XL4015 buck (servo 6.3 V)
components.spec: 24 V in, set 6.3 V out with a meter BEFORE connecting the servo (it can output up to 36 V)

components.label: Yaw motor (XY42STH40, base)
components.spec: NEMA 17, 1.2 A rated, run at 1.0 A

components.label: Shoulder motor (XY42STH40, turret)
components.spec: NEMA 17, 1.2 A rated, run at 1.0 A

components.label: Elbow motor (XY42STH40, lower shank)
components.spec: NEMA 17, 1.2 A rated, run at 1.0 A

components.label: Wrist motor (HEM-17D2008-10, upper shank)
components.spec: NEMA 17 34 mm, 0.8 A rated, run at 0.7 A

components.label: Yaw homing switch (KW12-3)
components.spec: SPDT roller lever, C + NO used, soldered leads

cables.label: 24 V: shield terminal to buck input
Z axis: yaw motor
cables.logic: STEP D4 · DIR D7 · EN D8

cables.label: Y axis: shoulder motor
cables.logic: STEP D3 · DIR D6 · EN D8

cables.label: X axis: elbow motor
cables.logic: STEP D2 · DIR D5 · EN D8

cables.label: A axis: wrist motor
cables.logic: STEP D12 · DIR D13 (A-axis jumpers fitted) · EN D8

cables.label: Yaw home switch: Z- (D11)
cables.logic: INPUT_PULLUP, LOW = pressed (cam over the switch for yaw < 0)

notes: Never power the servo from the Uno 5 V pin: it is fed only from the XL4015 (set 6.3 V with a meter first); its ground is also tied to an Uno GND through the signal lead.

Stepper wire colours vary by maker: find each coil pair with a meter (a few ohms between the two wires of a coil) and put one pair on 1A/1B, the other on 2A/2B. If an axis runs backwards, flip its DIR_INVERT in the firmware.
Fit the A-axis jumpers (D12/D13) on the shield; the spindle pins are then not available, which is why the servo is on A3.

Route the motor and servo cables to the zip-tie block on the base's -x edge, then as a free ~0.5 m service loop to the arm; turn the yaw by hand through -150..150 with the cables fitted before powering.
Read the shield's bulk capacitor (must be 35 V or more for 24 V) and the A4988 sense resistors before setting Vref.
